examples.text: This heat is stifling.

Nobody has shaved or changed clothes for a week, the heat stifles and the flies are everywhere. There is little water but we do not expect to be here long. This is not much of a letter, Jess. The mailbag goes down our trench once a day. I must finish because it stops for no one.

glosses: An act or state of being stifled.
The joint between the femur and tibia in the hind leg of various four-legged mammals, especially horses, corresponding to the knee in humans.
A bone disease of this region.
To cause (a dog, horse, or other four-legged mammal) to dislocate or sprain its stifle joint.
мять, превращать в комок, сдавливая

examples.text: У меня привычка комкать бумажки, лежащие на столе, порой даже нужные (машинально как-то).

glosses: перен., разг. наспех что-нибудь доделывать, сокращать, уродовать спешным и небрежным выполнением

examples.text: Фрадков запретил комкать бюджет.
Я решила нашу первую встречу не комкать и вовсе на неё не пошла.

glosses: мять, надавливать или сжимать, изменяя форму, комкать.
перен. подавлять, опрокидывать, преодолевать чьё-то сопротивление.

examples.text: Наступающие отряды сминают оборону противника.

glosses: A crease, wrinkle, or irregular fold.
To rumple; to press into wrinkles by crushing together.

examples.text: He crumpled the note and threw it away.

glosses: To cause to collapse.

examples.text: He crumpled the car's body panels when he backed into a post.

glosses: To become wrinkled.

examples.text: The car's body panels crumpled when they hit the post.

glosses: To collapse; to surrender.

examples.text: The team's defensive strategy crumpled.
The defenders crumpled owing to exhaustion and dehydration.

Yes, Juve were unfortunate, in the extreme, with the deflected goal from Casemiro that gave Madrid a 2-1 lead just after the hour. From that point onwards, however, it was staggering to see a team renowned for defensive structure crumple this way.

glosses: To work and press into a mass, usually with the hands; especially, to work, as by repeated pressure with the knuckles, into a well mixed mass, the materials of bread, cake, etc.

examples.text: Knead the dough by pressing down on it with the heels of both your palms and pushing it forward to stretch it, then pulling it back toward you...

glosses: To treat or form as if by kneading; to beat.

examples.text: I will knead him: I'll make him supple.

glosses: Of cats, to make an alternating pressing motion with the two front paws.

examples.text: Cats knead with their paws when happy, just as they kneaded when feeding from their mothers as kittens.
One of the most characteristic things that cats do is ”knead,” pushing their paws alternately against any invitingly soft area of their human friends' bodies like a baker kneading dough.

Why do cats knead? When kittens are nursing, they knead against their mothers' bellies to draw out milk. A relaxed adult cat kneads your leg or a couch cushion to show that he's happy and content, as he was when he was a nursing baby.

glosses: To mix thoroughly; form into a homogeneous compound.
The act of kneading something.

examples.text: Do not expect the dough to be very manageable even after a good knead.

glosses: Pétrir.

examples.text: Gnieść ciasto, pétrir la pâte.

glosses: Écraser, presser, oppresser.
